reality_delta: The claimed change is still a documentation update, and the main AI has added post-edit lifecycle/gate checks and an anti-loop boundary. main_concern: The evidence is still a set of file references and command summaries. A referenced excerpt/hash file is a receipt, not proof, unless its content is shown; the scoped git status intentionally excludes the broader worktree; and 'decision=optional' from the gate is ambiguous and weaker than explicit authorization.
top_risks: The excerpt, hash, and execution mapping may be incomplete, inconsistent, or not match the actual plan file because they are not inline.
Scoped git status does not prove that no runtime implementation files were changed in this refresh; it only checks the plan document and evidence directory.
The anti-loop boundary is a self-declared plan rule with no enforcement mechanism, so the next cycle could still reframe another gap as a 'new issue' and loop back into plan edits.
missing_evidence: The actual inline text of the added sections, the hash value, and the full open-item execution mapping table.
A worktree-wide git diff or status proving no RSP implementation/runtime files were modified during this refresh.
Clear semantics of the post-edit gate result: what 'decision=optional' means and whether it explicitly authorizes the bounded plan-only task.
minimum_fix: Inline the excerpt, hash, and execution mapping; provide a full worktree git diff or equivalent no-runtime-change verification; and explain the gate decision value so its authorization is unambiguous.

anti_loop_signal.reason: The next cycle must open with inline, auditable content and a full worktree diff, not another summary that says 'the plan now covers it.' If a gap remains, produce a concrete contract/check/runtime mapping, not another plan-only edit.
